key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the strongest task-specific predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while multitask neural networks offered competitive shared-learning performance across the related welding targets.
engineering_relevance: The study shows how predictive models can support welding process optimization by estimating mechanical outcomes that matter for joint integrity and quality control.
method: Compared multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Trained both approaches on the same welding dataset to predict UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated performance using RMSE and R² for each target.
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved RMSE/R² of 0.0263/0.9863 for UTS, 0.0467/0.9782 for weld hardness, and 0.1109/0.8453 for HAZ hardness, outperforming MTNN on individual-task accuracy.
watch_item: Results may depend on dataset size and weld-condition diversity, so external validation is needed before deploying the models in new welding settings.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
